## Why This Is Asked

This question tests practical implementation of CISSP risk-based access controls across multi-cloud environments, focusing on ABAC with policy-as-code, ephemeral credentials, runtime attestation, MFA, and continuous auditing. It also probes tooling choices and validation strategy at scale.

- ABAC
- policy-as-code
- OPA
- ephemeral credentials
- runtime attestation
- MFA
- SIEM

## Code Example

```javascript
// Example policy snippet (pseudo-OPA Rego)
package policy.authz

default allow = false

allow {
  input.subject.canAccess
  input.resource == 'dataLake:dataset'
  input.riskScore >= 5
  input.action in ['read','query']
}
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you measure risk score thresholds and adjust in production?
- What are failure modes for ephemeral credentials and how to mitigate?

```rego
default allow = false

allow {
    input.request.method == "GET"
    input.request.path == ["api", "v1", "resources"]
    input.user.role == "auditor"
    time.now_ns() < input.session.expiry
}

allow {
    input.request.method == "POST"
    input.request.path == ["api", "v1", "deploy"]
    input.user.role == "deployer"
    input.user.environment == input.request.environment
    is_approved_workflow(input.request.workflow_id)
}

is_approved_workflow(workflow_id) {
    workflow := data.workflows[workflow_id]
    workflow.status == "approved"
    workflow.approved_by != input.user.id
}
```
